description: Every automerge rule below deliberately leaves automergeType at its default, 'pr'.
Do not set it to 'branch'. A branch automerge pushes a Renovate branch with NO pull
request, and a repo whose required status checks trigger on `pull_request` therefore
never reports them on that branch — so branch protection can never be satisfied and
the update rebases nightly, forever. nicgpt lost six branches this way for up to 83
days (renovate/react, renovate/lock-file-maintenance, renovate/provider-runtime,
renovate/nextjs-monorepo, renovate/postcss-8.x, renovate/vitest), and the tell was
the dashboard's 'Pending Branch Automerge' section rather than any failure anywhere.
With 'pr', Renovate merges the PR itself once the branch is green, which works on
protected and unprotected repos alike — platformAutomerge stays off, see its commit.
The security fast-path. Until 2026-08-22 there was none: GitHub vulnerability
alerts were DISABLED on all 11 repos, so Renovate had no data source and could
not raise a security PR at all. A CVE therefore waited for the Monday window like
a cosmetic bump, and the nine `next` CVEs were fixed by a hand-rolled branch.
Alerts were enabled on all 11 repos on 2026-08-22; this block says what happens next.
schedule + minimumReleaseAge are overridden HERE deliberately: the Monday window and
the 7-day soak on next/react are right for routine bumps and wrong for a live CVE.
groupName below keeps the vitest packages in ONE security PR and leaves every other
security update exactly as it was. Ungrouping here is deliberate — one CVE per PR
lands the fix sooner — and it is only wrong for a package that pins its peers
EXACTLY, because then the ungrouped PR cannot install at all.
@vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.11 requires vitest@4.1.11: no caret, no range. When
CVE-2026-84373 hit vitest on 2026-09-10 it pulled vitest out of the group and left
@vitest/coverage-v8 behind in the ordinary one, so the pair became two PRs that each
changed only package.json. Renovate could not regenerate either lockfile, npm ci
failed ERESOLVE, and ci / baseline-rebuild-local / Vercel went red with it on
nicgpt #330 + #333, el-ifs #59 + #62, health #30 and learn #301. The CVE fix was
unlandable for five days because the PR carrying it could not merge.
WHY A TEMPLATE AND NOT A PLAIN NAME. Renovate spreads this whole block into a
`force` object on the rule it generates per advisory (process/vulnerabilities.ts),
and config/utils.ts ends every mergeChildConfig with `{ ...config, ...config.force }`.
So whatever this block says beats every packageRule below, and the inherited default
of groupName: null is precisely what ungroups the pair. Three things that look like
fixes are not, and two of them validate clean while doing nothing:
- a plain string here ('vitest') groups EVERY security update in every repo under
that one name — lodash and next were seen landing on renovate/vitest;
- a nested packageRules entry setting groupName is overwritten back to null by
that same force object on the next merge;
- `force` inside such a rule is globalOnly (options/index.ts:562) and is stripped
from a repository config with a warning.
The template is what makes it narrow: it is compiled per update, so only the vitest
packages get a group name at all.
THE ELSE BRANCH IS LOAD-BEARING — DO NOT SHORTEN IT TO ''. It reproduces Renovate's
default vulnerability branchTopic byte for byte, so every other security branch is
untouched (verified: lodash, next, @types/node, axios, @babel/core and socket.io all
keep renovate/npm-<dep>-vulnerability, with identical PR titles). An empty string
would NOT turn grouping off: branch-name.ts tests the raw template, which is always
truthy, then sets branchTopic to {{{groupSlug}}} — so every security update in the
repo would collapse onto one branch named `renovate/`.
vitest is the only group in this preset whose peers pin to one exact version;
react-dom asks for ^19.2.0 and eslint-config-next for ^7 || ^8 || ^9, and an
ungrouped security PR for either installs fine. Extend the test below only for a
package whose peer range is a single exact version. The name it emits must stay
identical to the vitest groupName in packageRules, or the pair splits again.
Group vitest packages. This name must stay identical to the one in the
vulnerabilityAlerts block above — the branch is renovate/{{groupSlug}}, so the
security update and the ordinary one share a PR only while both say 'vitest'.
Change one and you must change the other, or the pair splits again.
Without this rule the name comes from `group:monorepos` and is 'vitest monorepo',
while nicgpt's own renovate.json already calls it 'vitest'. Those two spellings
produced renovate/vitest-monorepo on el-ifs, health and learn and renovate/vitest
on nicgpt, so no single name in the block above could have rejoined the group on
all four repos. Naming it here makes the preset self-sufficient: a repo needs no
vitest rule of its own, and nicgpt's is now a duplicate that agrees.

description: GitHub Actions majors auto-merge on ci. Overrides the blanket major rule above
(later packageRules win), restoring EDR-0062 §6's tiering — 'dev/tooling/actions
-> auto-merge on ci; runtime libs -> dependency-gate; majors -> human'. The blanket
rule was holding actions majors too, which the tiering never intended: an actions
bump changes the CI runner, not shipped code, and ci proves it before merge.
